newsitem.title: VIETNAM: South Korea's Kim feted by communist Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's Kim feted by communist Vietnam.

text.p: South Korea's President Kim Young-sam arrived in Vietnam on Wednesday to a warm welcome for the leader of a country once considered a Cold War foe, but now embraced as a major investor.
Banners, flags and placards festooned key boulevards and intersections in Hanoi and local newspapers carried both official and unofficial messages of congratulation.
Kim was formally welcomed at the presidential palace by Communist Party chief Do Muoi.
His arrival in Vietnam marks the start of a nine-day swing through Southeast Asia that will include attending the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Manila.
Kim told journalists before leaving Seoul that the trip was aimed both at fostering economic relations and expediting the peace process on the Korean peninsula.

Full details of his agenda were not available on Wednesday, but diplomats said he was expected to sign agreements with Hanoi covering cooperation studies on nuclear energy and the establishment of Vietnam's first stock exchange.
But the immediate impact of his visit was symbolic.
Kim's is the first visit by a South Korean leader to Hanoi, and it comes just four years after ties were established.
Seoul and Hanoi fought on opposite sides during the Vietnam War, and Vietnam has ideological as well as other ties with communist North Korea.

But relations between the erstwhile foes have grown rapidly since 1992. Two-way trade currently stands at $1.54 billion a year, and South Korean firms have pledged some $2.3 billion towards projects in Vietnam.
Diplomats say Seoul considers strong links as crucial, not only because of Vietnam's economic revival but also because of regional strategic necessity.
Vietnam is now a member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and a prospective member of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
It also maintains relations with Pyongyang, although Vietnamese officials concede in private that influence has become limited as North Korea focuses increasingly on internal economic difficulties.
Kim held talks with Muoi at the Presidential Palace immediately following the welcoming ceremony, but details were not available.
He was due to meet Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and National Assembly chairman Nong Duc Manh on Thursday.
